stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Moderna and Merck say their mRNA cancer vaccine cut death, recurrence by 42%
stories.author: Beth Mole
bullet_points: Moderna and Merck reported top-line results for their mRNA cancer vaccine.
The vaccine demonstrated a significant efficacy rate, cutting death and recurrence by 42%.
This represents a major advancement in cancer immunotherapy using mRNA technology.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a language model.
The tags confirm its association with major AI frameworks like transformers and the Llama family.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is categorized for text-generation tasks.
Tags confirm its relevance within the transformers and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly gaining traction, serving a large developer base of 8.9 million.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when running through Ollama 0.31.
The speed improvement is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster, particularly when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Canva’s first AI image model plans designs before generating them
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Canva has launched 'Canva Craft,' its proprietary AI image generation model.
The model employs a two-stage architecture that plans designs before image generation.
This feature aims to offer users greater precision, consistency, and control compared to competitors like OpenAI and Google.

stories.title: Meta’s AI could still scrape news sites, legal experts say
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta's recent updates to its business terms aim to curb AI training on news sites.
Legal experts argue the changes are insufficient, pointing to ambiguous language allowing scraping.
The core concern remains Meta's ability to use content from news sites for AI model training.

stories.title: The FCC is beginning to block gadgets with ‘foreign surveillance chips’
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The FCC has gained the authority to block electronic gadgets containing chips deemed a national security threat.
This new power is being exercised for the first time, resulting in the blocking of two specific devices.
The FCC claims the blocked gadgets contain 'foreign surveillance chips.'

stories.title: Disgraced eMudhra drops out of TLS business after using cert private key of 4
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: eMudhra, a digital certificate authority, has withdrawn from the TLS business following a major security failure.
The vulnerability stemmed from a flawed key signing process that allowed unauthorized minting of web credentials.
This flaw effectively permitted the creation of valid web credentials for any website.

stories.title: Post-Audit Mirage: Identifiability Limits of Offline Agent Verification
stories.author: Payal Payal
bullet_points: Introduces the 'Post-Audit Mirage,' a critical flaw where offline safety tests fail to predict post-deployment agent behavior.
The research operationalizes this mirage by creating scenarios where verifier-visible evidence is identical for safe and harmful updates.
The work establishes a theoretical tradeoff between error rates and the ability to abstain from deployment based on observational equivalence.

stories.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
stories.author: Jianfei Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'LongZero,' a method to enhance long-context reasoning in LLMs without relying on extensive, expensive training data.
Addresses the major bottleneck in RL-based LLM improvement: the scarcity and high cost of generating long, diverse, and verifiable training data.
Proposes an 'RL from zero data' approach to overcome dependencies on external corpora or stronger teacher models.

stories.title: Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation with Preference Feedback
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy vulnerability in Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) by integrating Differential Privacy (DP).
The research tackles a limitation in existing private alignment methods, which typically assume dense reward parameterizations.
Proposes a method for Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation, aiming to reduce estimation error bounds that currently scale prohibitively with model size.

stories.title: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale
stories.author: johnbender
bullet_points: LLMs are enabling formal software verification at a significantly larger scale.
This suggests a major advancement in the intersection of AI and software engineering.
The feasibility of verifying complex software systems is being fundamentally changed by LLM capabilities.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Cloudflare's 27B multimodal decision model, Clef, is now accessible via Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or through Ollama's cloud infrastructure.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful, large-scale multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now available on Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is offered for free for a limited time via Ollama Cloud.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of its cloud models for AI agents.
The integration allows AI agents to run safely within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure deployment of AI agents in the cloud.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Etsy is cracking down on AI slop listings
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Etsy is implementing stricter guidelines regarding the use of AI in product listings.
The crackdown aims to reduce the proliferation of low-quality, AI-generated content ('AI slop') on the platform.
The policy change is driven by buyer feedback and seller concerns about the quality and authenticity of listings.

stories.title: Spotify says yes, it is busting people for using Family Plan sharing too widely
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Spotify is implementing a new QR code verification system to combat unauthorized sharing of its Family Plan.
The crackdown targets users who are not actually residing together under the Family Plan.
Spotify co-CEO Alex Norström confirmed the initiative during the company's recent earnings call.

stories.title: PC shipments dropped over 20 percent in Q3 due to RAM price hikes
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Global PC shipments experienced a significant decline of 21% year-over-year in Q3 2026.
The drop in PC demand is attributed to ongoing price increases, particularly in RAM.
Smartphone shipments also saw a notable decrease, reaching a 14-year low in the same quarter.

stories.title: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Security vulnerability discovered in the upcoming Switch 2 console.
The exploit, a 'userland' vulnerability, leverages an integer overflow in the SmileBasic interpreter.
This allows hackers to gain unauthorized homebrew access to the system.

stories.title: Electric or gas? BMW goes both ways with new 2027 X5 and iX5.
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: BMW is offering a dual-powertrain strategy for the 2027 X5 and iX5.
The electric variant boasts a substantial 450-mile range.
The EV model supports a high-speed charging rate of 460 kW.

stories.title: Samsung all but confirms iPhone Duo is goosing Galaxy Z8 sales
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: The unveiling of the 'iPhone Duo' has correlated with a surge in searches for Samsung foldables.
This suggests a potential competitive impact of Apple's new device on Samsung's foldable market share.
The article points to a direct market reaction following a major competitor's product launch.

stories.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Chaim Baskin
bullet_points: Addresses unique quantization challenges in Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) due to their iterative denoising process.
Demonstrates that quantization sensitivity is dependent on both the downstream task and the specific denoising timestep.
Introduces T2Quant, a mixed-precision technique that predicts these sensitivity patterns without requiring ground truth labels.

stories.title: When More Metadata Misleads: Probing Field-Level Grounding in LLM-Generated Museum Descriptions
stories.author: Laura Hollink
bullet_points: The research investigates how metadata influences the quality of text generation (specifically museum descriptions) by challenging the assumption that more metadata always improves grounding.
It addresses the complexity of real-world museum catalogue records, noting their heterogeneity, partial visual nature, and uneven documentation.
The study employs a two-phase framework to analyze how varying metadata composition affects the generated artifact descriptions.

stories.title: Prompting Strategy Effects Depend on the Judge: A Multilingual Study of LLM-as-a-Judge Robustness
stories.author: Clemencia Siro
bullet_points: The study investigates the robustness of LLM-as-a-Judge evaluations across different languages and judge models.
It addresses a gap where prompting strategies (like CoT) are often optimized only for English benchmarks and their cross-lingual transfer is unknown.
The research measures the interaction between prompting strategies and judge model sensitivity in multilingual tasks.

stories.title: Network topology shapes consensus and vulnerability in LLM populations
stories.author: Luca Maria Aiello
bullet_points: The study investigates how the interaction structure (network topology) influences the collective behavior of interacting Large Language Models (LLMs).
It moves beyond traditional 'well-mixed' interaction models by testing LLM consensus formation on different network structures (fully connected, random regular, heterogeneous).
The research demonstrates that network topology significantly impacts the speed and even the possibility of consensus emerging within the LLM population.

stories.title: Prompt Sensitivity in Tool-Augmented Model Comparisons
stories.author: Tomasz Radzikowski
bullet_points: Investigates prompt sensitivity when comparing tool-augmented language models.
Highlights that simple accuracy gains don't reveal stability issues introduced by tool usage.
Proposes a novel 'matched protocol' to decouple and analyze specific steps in tool-augmented reasoning (e.g., decision to call, tool output).

stories.title: PriMa-Causa: Causal Prescriptive Maintenance
stories.author: Felix Saretzky
bullet_points: Introduces 'PriMa-Causa,' a framework for Causal Prescriptive Maintenance in automated manufacturing.
Addresses the challenge of making data-driven decisions under uncertainty and sparse data.
Moves beyond mere prediction by recommending specific, actionable maintenance interventions.

stories.title: Mixing Matters: Evidence Position Bias Across Sequence Mixers in Long-Context Question Answering
stories.author: Mehul Anand
bullet_points: The research investigates position bias in long-context Question Answering across different model architectures (Transformer, State-Space, Mamba).
Transformers exhibit a 'beginning advantage,' while state-space models lack this, but both favor evidence appearing near the end of the context.
The findings suggest that how models process evidence location is architecture-dependent, impacting long-context performance.

stories.title: SetCommit: Coordinated Token Commitments for Few-Step Diffusion Language Model Decoding
stories.author: Wang Kang
bullet_points: Introduces SetCommit, a training-free method for coordinating parallel token commitments in diffusion language models.
Addresses the challenge of joint inconsistency in tokens generated in parallel during few-step decoding.
Aims to balance token reliability with the need for context-dependent refinement during the decoding process.

stories.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
stories.author: Jun Xu
bullet_points: Proposes Item-Level Adaptive Recursion to improve sequential recommendation models.
Challenges the standard practice of allocating a fixed computational budget to all historical items.
Identifies that item computational needs are non-uniform, with some requiring deep processing while others converge quickly.

stories.title: BatchBench: Benchmarking AI Robustness to Batch Effects and Domain Shift in Biomedical Images - A JUMP Cell Painting Leaderboard
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces BatchBench, a new leaderboard designed to benchmark AI robustness in biomedical imaging.
Addresses the critical issue of domain shift and batch effects, which significantly degrade AI performance in real-world medical imaging scenarios.
Highlights that despite progress in domain adaptation, substantial performance gaps remain in handling variations across different experimental conditions.

stories.title: When More Metadata Misleads: Probing Field-Level Grounding in LLM-Generated Museum Descriptions
stories.author: Laura Hollink
bullet_points: Investigates the limitations of metadata-conditioned generation in Large Language Models (LLMs) when applied to museum descriptions.
Highlights that the heterogeneity and uneven documentation of museum catalogue records challenge the assumption that more metadata always improves grounding.
Proposes a two-phase framework to analyze how varying metadata composition influences the quality of AI-generated artifact descriptions.

stories.title: Prompting Strategy Effects Depend on the Judge: A Multilingual Study of LLM-as-a-Judge Robustness
stories.author: Clemencia Siro
bullet_points: Investigates the robustness of LLM-as-a-Judge evaluations across different languages and judge models.
Addresses a gap where prompting strategies (like Chain-of-Thought) are often optimized only for English benchmarks.
Tests how prompt sensitivity interacts with the choice of judge model and language in multilingual NLP tasks.

stories.title: Beyond Watching and Searching: Benchmarking Agents for Video-centered Deep Research Reports
stories.author: Yunhai Tong
bullet_points: Introduces a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents in deep research.
Focuses on video-centered research, moving beyond simple web searching.
Agents synthesize multimodal evidence from external sources into interactive reports linked to specific video moments.

stories.title: Mixing Matters: Evidence Position Bias Across Sequence Mixers in Long-Context Question Answering
stories.author: Mehul Anand
bullet_points: The study investigates position bias in long-context question answering models, showing that evidence effectiveness degrades when placed far from prompt boundaries.
Transformer models exhibit a 'beginning advantage,' while state-space models (like Mamba) lack this, but both favor evidence appearing near the end.
The findings provide comparative insights into how different architectures (Transformer vs. Mamba) handle positional information in long-context processing.

stories.title: Learning What to Ask for Tomorrow: Active Preference Acquisition for Long-Term Personalized Web Agents
stories.author: Taotao Cai
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of passive memory in long-term personalized web agents by focusing on preference acquisition.
Introduces Active Preference Acquisition (APA) to proactively learn user preferences that are not explicitly revealed.
Overcomes the flaw in current clarification methods that only consider immediate task benefit, aiming for long-term utility.

stories.title: RIFT: KV Cache Compression for Draft Models with Complementary Compressibility Training
stories.author: Ran Zilberstein
bullet_points: The research addresses the growing memory bottleneck of the KV cache in long-output generation, particularly when using speculative decoding.
It introduces 'decode staleness,' a problem where compression methods optimized for initial (prefill) context lose accuracy as the output sequence lengthens.
The proposed method, RIFT, utilizes 'Complementary Compressibility Training' to improve KV cache compression specifically for draft models.

stories.title: OpenShell – A safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents
stories.author: niemandhier
bullet_points: Introduction of OpenShell, a new runtime environment.
Designed specifically for managing fleets of autonomous AI agents.
Emphasizes safety and privacy within the AI agent ecosystem.

stories.title: Run full iOS 16.5 firmware on Android Devices
stories.author: aghuang
bullet_points: A new method allows running full iOS 16.5 firmware on Android devices.
This represents a significant achievement in cross-platform emulation or system modification.
The announcement is posted on Hacker News, suggesting a technical/developer audience.

stories.title: Building Disaggregated Inference with NVIDIA Dynamo
stories.author: sharmukh
bullet_points: NVIDIA Dynamo is an open-source inference framework.
It is designed specifically for deploying large-scale generative AI models.
The framework focuses on enabling disaggregated inference capabilities.
